title: Y lagging behind drew a chunk of bread from under his foreboard, crammed it into his mouth and munched as he walked.
html_source: This is a classic example of James Joyce’s predilection for punning and literary ‘easter eggs.’ While on the surface this line is merely a comical, if quotidian, image, it is particularly notable for the crossing over of the “Y” and the “S” in “H.E.L.Y.S.” The first word of Ulysses is “stately” and the last Molly Bloom’s emphatic, feminine “Yes”, one starting with “s” and one “y.” Therefore, the “s” and the “y” must at some point cross over and here, the middle of the book, 12:00 noon, is where this happens. While this is likely meant as a simple structural nuance, perhaps not conveying any great meaning, it is nonetheless interesting to see how Joyce’s overarching scheme for the novel fits together.
